stem: Aarav blows exhaled air through lime water in a test tube, and his teacher Meera passes inhaled (fresh) air through lime water in a second test tube. Only the lime water with exhaled air turns milky. What should Aarav correctly conclude from this experiment?

options.text: Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air, but it still contains some oxygen.
Lime water turning milky shows that exhaled air contains oxygen.
Inhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than exhaled air.
Exhaled air contains no oxygen at all.

teacher.key_rationale: Lime water turning milky is a test for carbon dioxide, so only the exhaled-air tube turning milky shows exhaled air has more carbon dioxide than inhaled air; the body does not use all inhaled oxygen, so exhaled air still contains oxygen. B reverses the meaning of the milky test, C reverses the comparison, and D wrongly claims exhaled air has no oxygen.
